children: U.S. farmers are seen as selling into the sizable long positions held by managed money in grain futures, locking in prices that are more supportive for their budgets. This is seen particularly in corn, according to Charlie Sernatinger of Marex in a note. He says corn futures are lower due to "farmer selling and funds being loaded long already." In its latest Commitments of Traders report the CFTC said managed money funds were net long corn futures by 431,062 contracts. Total long positions are at nearly 500,000 contracts, according to the CFTC. Most-active corn futures are down 0.7%, while soybeans are up 0.1% and wheat rises 0.7%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
